title: Climate action update, community grants and local development approvals
subtitle: Heritage designation, Erinbrook Drive traffic safety, community centre expansion, green development standards, Committee of Adjustment appointment and land sale.
overview: Council heard from local climate organizations about the region's 2019 and 2020 greenhouse gas re-inventory. Delegates reported that transportation remains the largest source of emissions, and that the 2020 drop was driven largely by the pandemic.

Council then approved a series of reports. These include $198,137 in Tier 2 community grants {{vote:m4}}, all-way stops and speed cushions on Erinbrook Drive {{vote:m8}}, and moving the Mill Courtland Community Centre expansion to detailed design {{vote:m7}}. Staff will also start Phase 2 of the Green Development Standards project {{vote:m6}}, and a notice to designate 369 Frederick Street as a heritage property will be published {{vote:m2}}.

Council approved official plan and zoning changes for 265 Cotton Grass Street {{vote:m10}} and 7 Morrison Road {{vote:m11}}. It also appointed a returning member to the Committee of Adjustment despite the policy's one-year gap {{vote:m13}}. After a closed session, Council authorized the sale of a surplus part of the Tagge Street right-of-way for a noise wall easement {{vote:m14}}. The Mayor will raise the Lancaster Street ramp and the cancelled GRT Route 2 with Regional Council.

decisions.detail: Council approved $198,137 in Tier 2 community grants and moved several named organizations to the Tier 1 process for 2024.
Council approved all-way stops at two intersections and two speed cushions, and directed a pedestrian crossover study for the area.
Council received the business case and directed staff to proceed to the detailed design phase of the expansion.
Council directed staff to start Phase 2 of the Green Development Standards project and report back with a recommendation.
Council adopted an official plan amendment, to be forwarded to the Region for approval, and approved the related zoning change.
Council adopted an official plan amendment, approved the zoning change and adopted the urban design brief for use in site plan approval.
The Clerk was directed to publish a notice of intention to designate the property under the Ontario Heritage Act.
Council appointed Bob McColl to the Committee of Adjustment until November 14, 2024, despite the policy's one-year lapse requirement.

debate: Delegates said transportation of goods and people is the largest emissions source and still rising. They noted that 2019 data suggests the 2020 target was met mainly because of the pandemic.

In response to councillors' questions, delegates said the inventory leaves out flights and the embodied carbon of building materials. They said a net-positive office building cost only modestly more than a standard green-certified one.

One councillor raised concern that provincial investment in natural gas generation could make the electricity grid dirtier. Delegates said advocacy to other levels of government is part of the regional strategy, since local action alone cannot reach the 2030 target.

On the Committee of Adjustment appointment, one councillor asked why a returning member was chosen over other applicants, given the term-limit policy. Staff said the nominating committee preferred someone with experience.

Councillors asked the Mayor to raise the cancelled GRT Route 2 and its lack of community engagement with Regional Council. One councillor also asked whether traffic impacts of the Lancaster ramp closures have been made clear to residents.
